text: Not bones in a museum. [pause] Not a movie. [pause] Living, breathing giants… sharing the planet with you.
To see how, we have to go back sixty-six million years.
A rock about ten kilometres wide is racing towards Earth at twenty kilometres per second.
In our history, it hits. [pause] Three out of every four species vanish.
But Earth moves fast through space. [pause] If that rock had arrived just a few minutes later… it would have missed.
One kilometre. [pause] Across the river, a herd of long-necks keeps on eating, as if nothing happened.
Forty metres. [pause] Triceratops, around ten tonnes each, wade in to drink.
Back then, our ancestors were tiny. [pause] Small furry mammals, hiding in the ferns.
Most scientists think we would never have appeared at all.
But imagine we did. [pause] And imagine we tried to keep them… behind a fence.
